questions.title: Cigarettes sold per adult per day in the United States
questions.hint: This century brought higher tobacco taxes, indoor smoking bans, and the rise of e-cigarettes.
questions.explanation: It fell to 2.4 in 2020, from 5.7 in 2000.

source.attribution: US CDC, Office on Smoking and Health

questions.title: Pupils per teacher in public schools in the United States
questions.unitLabel: pupils per full-time-equivalent teacher, public elementary and secondary schools
questions.hint: This divides all pupils by all teachers, including specialist and special-education teachers, so it is not the same as class size.
questions.explanation: It fell to 15.4 in 2020, from 25.8 in 1960. Each year is the school year that starts in the autumn of that year.

source.attribution: US National Center for Education Statistics

questions.title: Corn harvested per acre in the United States
questions.unitLabel: bushels of corn for grain per harvested acre
questions.hint: Hybrid seed, fertilizer and machinery all arrived at different times; a drought can still wreck one year.
questions.explanation: It rose to 187 in 2025, from 74 in 1965.

questions.title: Proved crude oil reserves in the United States
questions.unitLabel: billion barrels, at the end of each year
questions.hint: Proved reserves are oil that can be produced at today’s prices with today’s technology, so they move with both.
questions.explanation: It rose to 35.8 in 2020, from 7.2 in 1920.

questions.title: New homes started each year in the United States
questions.unitLabel: million new privately owned housing units started
questions.hint: Builders start more homes when mortgages are cheap and fewer in recessions, while the population keeps growing.
questions.explanation: It went from 1.47 in 1965 to a high of 2.07 in 2005, then ended at 1.36 in 2025. Counts houses and each apartment in a building separately, from the Census Bureau and HUD Survey of Construction.
